about: Every source behind the Town app's Streets tab: permits, sales, the blotter and construction projects, with fields and the rules scripts/town/streets.py applies.

sources.name: City permits export: Building (OpenGov)
sources.how: where ApplicationDate >= DATE 'YYYY-MM-DD', all fields; 143,898 records back to the portal's start.
sources.cadence: City re-exports roughly weekly; last export 2026-10-20 (DataUpdateDate)
fields: PermitNo (prefix = type: CBP building, CEP electrical, CMP mechanical, CPP plumbing, SIGN, DECK, FENC, WIN, RS, CHU)
PrimaryLUC (land use: R1 single family ... C commercial, CR com/resident, I industrial, E exempt)
sources.notes: Weekly list: group ApplicationDate by ISO week (streets.json permits.weekly_roundup). Notable rule, applied to CBP and Z* permits: demolition (not interior), ADU, commercial-use restaurant/bar/cafe/bakery/brewery/coffee/catering or tenant fit-out or change of use, new building or 10+ units; any permit with estimated cost >= $250,000. On Oct 29 this tagged 15 of 519 permits from the last six weeks. A map needs the addresses geocoded (Vermont's E911 geocoder or the city parcel layer).

sources.name: City permits export: Zoning
sources.how: Same schema and query as Building; 36,404 records.
sources.notes: Prefixes ZP zoning permit, ZCO certificate of occupancy, ZPS/ZPF/ZPW/ZPR/ZPD/ZAP/ZSP sub-types (meanings not published in the export; read one record in the portal to label them).

sources.name: City permits export: Fire Marshal
sources.how: Same schema; 7,061 records: sprinkler permits, time-of-sale inspections, etc.
sources.notes: Low value for the column; RTOS (residential time-of-sale) records could pre-signal sales.

sources.name: Right-of-way excavation and obstruction permits
sources.how: 1,376 records with real lat/long, but last edited 2025-12-10.
sources.notes: Would feed 'Torn up' (who is digging where) if DPW resumes the export; ask DPW.

sources.name: OpenGov permitting portal
sources.how: No public API; each permit's PublicUrl opens its record.
sources.notes: For the freshest permits (after the weekly export) a person would search the portal by hand.

sources.name: Public Notice of Permit Applications
sources.how: Read when a big project is pending; notice periods and appeals.

sources.name: Vermont property transfer tax returns (VT Property Transfers)
sources.publisher: Vermont Department of Taxes via VCGI
sources.how: where TOWNNAME='BURLINGTON' AND closeDate >= DATE 'YYYY-MM-DD'. 6,865 Burlington returns in the layer; posts about a week after closing; layer last edited 2026-10-27.
fields: blCn1Desc (class: 02 single family, 05 condo, 06 multi-family, 09 office, 10 retail, 12 gas station, 20 other)
bUsePrDesc / sUsePrDesc (buyer and seller use: principal residence, long-term rental, commercial...)
sources.notes: Item page: https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=91afc67976d54f9c86437c4fe8744e03. Rules in streets.py: arm's length = fee simple, no exemption, price > 0. Notable = commercial class or use, price >= $1M, multi-family >= $750K, entity buyer, or out-of-state buyer (buyer mailing state not VT). Running medians at 30/90/365 days and by month for single family, condo and all residential. Oct 29: 90-day median $507,500 (77 sales), 365-day out-of-state share 11.6%.

sources.name: Burlington Assessor's Office
sources.how: Parcel cards are not exposed as an API; the PTTR layer already carries the grand list value.
sources.notes: BTV_Parcel_Owners_2019 on the city ArcGIS is a 2019 snapshot (last edited 2023) and not used.

sources.name: Property Taxes by parcel
sources.how: 217,350 rows: TaxYear, TaxParcelId, SPAN, IsHomestead, Land/Building/RealValue, PropertyTaxAmount. Joins to PTTR by SPAN.
sources.notes: Lets the sold list show the last tax bill; also powers City Hall's tax-bill page.

sources.name: BPD press releases (News Flash, Police)
sources.how: Headline, date, link and case number (NNBU######) kept; release bodies are not copied because they can name people.
sources.notes: The weekly written column is a records-reading routine: open each release, write it up, name a person only if the release says they were arrested or charged (Stephen's rule), never victims or people merely questioned.

sources.name: BPD incidents (calls for service), monthly export
sources.how: Layer id changes each month (151 for the Oct 1 export); script reads the service root for the current id. call_time is a text field, so the month filter is LIKE 'YYYY-MM%'.
sources.cadence: Monthly, about a month behind (latest call 2026-09-30)
sources.notes: No names. 2,620 calls in September 2026. There is no public daily log; the old Police_Incident_Log layer stops in 2013.

sources.name: BPD arrests, monthly export
sources.how: Same monthly re-publish pattern; latest arrest 2026-08-31.
sources.notes: No names. Counts by category only in streets.json; age/race not copied into the app by default (Stephen's call).

sources.name: Burlington Fire Department incidents, monthly export
sources.notes: For the 'police and fire' column's fire half: counts and response times. Notable fires come through city news releases.

sources.name: BTVstat open data hub
sources.how: Human-readable dataset pages and dashboards for the exports above.

sources.name: Construction portal layer (CIP, all combined)
sources.publisher: City of Burlington (DPW, Parks, BED, CEDO)
sources.how: All 1,815 segments; grouped by PROJNAME into 690 projects; streets.json keeps those not completed/cancelled more than a year ago (208 on Oct 29).
fields: CIPSTAT (Proposed, In Design, Approved/In-Design, Under Construction, Postponed, Completed, Canceled)
sources.notes: One page per project = one record in streets.json projects.items (slug, status, streets, wards, dates, contact, links). Since You Checked already logs edits to this layer as change lines.

sources.name: See, Click, Fix (city issue reporting)
sources.how: For the Report tab: the city's own reporting tool; check whether SeeClickFix's public API covers Burlington before building a separate pin-and-photo board.
sources.notes: Stephen's call: link to the city's tool or run a separate public board.
